raw_response:
I farm 65 mu with only three people in the household, so I have to keep the plan tight and manageable. I will keep wheat-maize as my backbone because it fits my land, my well irrigation, and what I know best after 25 years. I will put most of the land into winter wheat followed by summer maize, because that gives me steady grain and spreads risk. I will still keep cabbage, chili, stevia, and watermelon, but on smaller blocks because they need more labor and closer watching. I will use improved or hybrid seed on the crops where it clearly helps me with stand, uniformity, and yield. I will not push fertilizer blindly; I will feed the grain crops steadily and give the cash crops enough to hold yield and quality without making the field too lush. With well irrigation, I will water at key growth stages instead of too often. For tillage, I will mostly use rotary tillage because it matches my equipment and labor situation, while chili I will keep under plough tillage to make a better root zone. I will control pests in a practical way: fewer sprays on wheat and maize, more on chili, cabbage, and watermelon because those crops are easier to lose if I react too late.
